listen: Good morning. This is The Daily Brief for Saturday, November 21. Here is what matters today. The lead story is on Wall Street. The S&P 500 fell 3.7 percent on Friday. The Nasdaq composite is now negative for the year. AI stocks have very large market values, so they have a much bigger effect on the market's direction. They drove this year's big gains. Now they are behind the slide. Now the front page. In tech, Levent Alpöge says he and Claude discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis. He says the method extends to the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis, and that they formalized the argument. A separate note from Ravi Vakil describes another proposed proof that is reportedly all human, with no AI. At the United Nations, talks in Geneva on AI-powered killer robots and drones ended with no firm commitment. Nations agreed to extend the discussions for two more years. In sports, Nikola Jokic had 26 points, 11 assists and seven rebounds. Denver beat the Houston Rockets 133 to 124 in an NBA Cup game. In Washington, President Trump held a press conference after his trip to Asia. NPR reports he offered few concrete results from the meetings with Xi and Putin, beyond a joint statement on unity over some issues. Now the sections. In tech, Anthropic announced the closing of its initial public offering. A trending GitHub project offers a skills framework for coding agents. In politics, a second federal judge said she will block Trump's arch with a preliminary injunction. Congress also needs a funding measure to avoid a shutdown next month, and Democrats aim to block funding for the Iran war. In world news, countries at the COP31 climate talks are deadlocked over fossil fuels. The FBI is reportedly investigating an apparent hack of a national criminal database. Zelensky called Putin a killer after Trump called the Russian leader a friend. In sports, the 49ers rule no one out for Sunday's game against the Vikings in Mexico. The Braves tendered contracts to four players. And UFC fighter Manon Fiorot got a three-month ban for violating the anti-doping policy. In Atlanta, a housing development broke ground near Topgolf and The Works. Street repaving began in Buckhead. And the Westside Future Fund broke ground on two affordable housing projects. In architecture, a new BIM platform called Pliera aims to challenge Revit. Rayon version four adds an AI agent to browser-based CAD. In science and nature, Pacific Ocean waters reached historic highs in 2026. The United States auctioned American Samoan seabed for mining, despite a court ruling that found the sale illegal. And conservation is bringing seabirds back to Lundy Island. That is the brief. Have a good day.

lead.title: S&P 500 sinks 3.7% and the Nasdaq composite goes negative for the year
lead.note: The S&P 500 fell 3.7% on Friday, and the Nasdaq composite is now negative for the year. According to the report, AI stocks carry very large market values, so they have a much bigger effect on which way the market moves. The same stocks were responsible for Wall Street's big gains this year, and they are now behind the sharp slide. That makes this more than a one-day drop. It shows how much of the market's performance has rested on a single theme. For a reader who works with AI tools and follows the companies behind them, it is a useful reminder that market swings in this sector can be large in both directions. The summary does not say what triggered the decline, so the cause is not yet clear from this item.
